newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher despite CPI worries.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher despite CPI worries.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Thursday in what traders said was a technical rebound from the declines of the last few days, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.24 percent, or 3.69 points, to 301.36 on an all-share turnover of 120 million shekels against 156 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.17 percent higher at 308.11.
"Today was a correction to the falls yesterday while the market awaits publication of the CPI on Friday," said Baruch Glicksberg, investment manager for an institutional investor.

"There is a lot of uncertainty in the market about the CPI. No one knows what it will be. Estimates are that it will be up by 1.0 to 1.2 percent, and that the central bank will raise interest rates by 0.5 percentage point at the end of the month," Glicksberg said.
The base rate stands now at 12.7 percent on an annual basis, where it has been since mid-June.
"Today they introduced continuous trading and it seems to have gone well," said Doron Zur, head of trading at Sahar Securities said.
"The shares that were included in the continuous trading got a lot of attention today, and trading volumes were good," Glicksberg said.

The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Thursday launched the first phase of a programme to introduce continuous, order-driven trading. The system, which started with 10 securities, is expected to eventually include all heavy capitalisation shares and bonds.
It replaces the "semi-continous" system in which shares are traded in rounds over the course of the day.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries rose 2.75 percent to 20,496 agorot following its rise on Wall Street on Wednesday, Glicksberg said.
"The negative sentiment about this share is over and most traders now feel the negative sentiment was not justified and have started buying the shares," Glicksberg said.

Bank Hapoalim fell 2.25 percent to 796 agorot on a newspaper report that external consultants to MI Holdings, the government company in charge of privatising Israeli banks, had valued the bank at as much as nine billion shekels. That is lower than Hapolaim's 10.2 billion shekel market capitalisation.
Clal Electronics Industries rose 3.75 percent to 52,963 agorot. Traders said the share had risen following the better-than-expected second-quarter results of its Scitex Corp affiliate on Monday.
Scitex reported a net profit of $157,000 in the second quarter after several quarters of sharp losses.
The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, with volume of 8.4 million shekels; Teva, with volume of 6.2 million shekels; and Formula Systems with volume 4.7 billion shekels.

Formula, which is one of the 10 shares in the continous trading system, rose 370 agorot to 7,680 agorot. In the continous trading system, price changes are reported in agorot rather than in percentages.
Traders said the heavy trading in Formula was due to its inclusion in the new-trading system.
($1 = 3.53 shekels)
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
